comparator.name: Political Science / Politicologie
comparator.academicYear: Current UvA published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. The generic target offers five second-year core-module specialisations. International Relations is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, before UCR course selection. The first-listed Sustainability Politics option is likewise used for the 6-EC year-2 restricted elective. Year 3 preserves the published seminar and thesis choices plus 30 EC of genuinely open elective/minor/internship/exchange space. The English and bilingual tracks have identical content.

components.name: Restricted-choice elective: Sustainability politics — Paradigms and debates
components.note: The first-listed official year-2 elective is selected as a neutral tie-break.

components.name: Free-choice electives: Optional subjects
components.note: Genuine open choice space within or outside Political Science; no particular minor, internship or exchange course is assumed.

questionsApplications.label: How do democratic and authoritarian institutions organise power and representation?
Why do political actors conflict or cooperate across states and global institutions?
How can governments design and evaluate policy responses to inequality and global challenges?

alternatives.concept: Combines comparative politics, political thought, international relations, law, sociology, communication and research methods to analyse power, institutions, democracy, inequality and political change. It is the broadest and closest feasible UCR response to the UvA degree.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum gives sustained weight to interstate relations, international law, conflict, security, global institutions and peace.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest plan, this route replaces political communication, constitutional comparison and some domestic social-change courses with international history, criminal justice, security, human rights and conflict-oriented psychology. Six courses differ and the organising question becomes international conflict and governance.

alternatives.concept: Builds from the official Public Policy and Governance and Political Economy directions, combining national institutions, comparative government, public economics, macro- and microeconomics, econometrics, law, data and policy communication.

alternatives.labelRationale: The plan centres how governments make, finance, communicate and evaluate policy under economic and institutional constraints.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This route replaces much of the closest and international-conflict curricula with economics, econometrics, data science, public administration, national political communication and policy research. It differs from each earlier plan by well over 30 EC and prioritises governance and policy evaluation.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic bachelor has five official core-module specialisations and none is identified as the broad default. The official International Relations and Public Policy/Political Economy directions support two further coherent and mechanically distinct curricula. All three pass current UCR feasibility checks, so production stops at the maximum of three.
